journey.intro: I don't have a corporate track record yet, but I have a journey. Each stage unlocked the kit for the next one.

noManual.title: No manual
noManual.description: Before I ever wrote code, I was already taking computers apart just to understand how they worked inside. Around 2009 I would open machines that were working fine, pull the RAM, poke at the boards with no idea what static electricity was, then try to put it all back together. It usually ended in getting grounded, and two computers didn't survive my curiosity.

mp3Tags.title: MP3s, tags, and Windows
mp3Tags.description: I used to download music from the old 4shared, and a lot of MP3s came with messy names or missing metadata. Windows Media Player would often show 'Unknown Artist', 'Unknown Album', and tracks out of order. I started researching how to rename files and edit MP3 ID3 tags to organize my library. Without realizing it, that's where I had my first contact with file editing and started understanding how Windows handled them.

cheatEngine.title: Memory and processes
cheatEngine.description: In 2015, looking for ways to boost my team's budget in FIFA, I found tools like Cheat Engine. I started searching for values in the game's memory, changing numbers at runtime, and understanding, even without knowing the terms yet, concepts like processes, memory addresses, and data manipulation. It was my first more technical contact with what was going on behind a program.

linuxAndServers.title: Linux, networks, and servers
linuxAndServers.description: Between 2016 and 2018, running game servers to play with friends turned into a hobby. I configured ports, IPs, and permissions, and kept an old PC running for hours. It was my first hands-on contact with Linux, networking, services, and server administration.

firstItJobs.title: First IT jobs
firstItJobs.description: In 2018, after finishing a hardware course, I started taking my first IT jobs. I did system reinstalls, memory upgrades, HDD-to-SSD swaps, power supply replacements, and computer maintenance for a few clients. That's when what had been curiosity and a hobby started turning into professional experience.

devAndIt.title: Development and IT
devAndIt.description: In 2023, I started diving deeper into programming, building sites with HTML and CSS and studying Python and programming logic. Today I work in IT at an accounting firm, where I develop systems for internal use and directly support the CEO, who also leads the IT area, with the maintenance, evolution, and support of the systems the firm uses. Development is where I found the area I feel most comfortable, motivated, and fulfilled in.

nextStep.title: Next step
nextStep.description: I want to take the next step by moving fully into development and/or support, putting into practice everything I've been building over the years. The next stage is still open, but the goal is clear: grow professionally in IT, learn from real projects, and keep evolving.

about.brief: I'm Pedro, a Software Engineering student and developer. My curiosity for technology goes back to playing video games as a kid, and it never stopped.
paragraphs: I currently work in IT at an accounting firm, handling support and building internal systems, while diving deeper into programming: HTML, CSS, Python, and the logic behind all of it.
I like projects that solve a real problem, clean code, and picking up new tools without fear. I treat every bug like a hard level: annoying in the moment, satisfying once it's cleared.
I'm in my 6th semester of Software Engineering at Unopar, with IT work in my day to day and the next step in mind: moving fully into development.

experience.empty: No formal work experience yet, I'm just starting that journey. In the meantime, take a look at my projects.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data this site collects, what it's used for, and your rights, in line with Brazil's LGPD (Law 13.709/2018).

sections.heading: 1. Who processes the data
sections.body: Pedro Teixeira, an individual, is the controller responsible for personal data on this site. Privacy requests and data subject requests are handled at contato@pedrotx.com.br.

sections.heading: 2. Legal basis for processing
sections.body: Contact form data is used to respond to inquiries, based on the legitimate interest in handling incoming requests (LGPD art. 7, IX), while respecting data subject rights. Submitting the form does not authorize advertising. Google cookies and campaign identifiers require consent (art. 7, I). Cookieless operational metrics and abuse prevention serve the legitimate interest in keeping the site available and secure.

sections.heading: 3. Data collected by the contact form
sections.body: Name, email, reason for contact, and message, submitted by you through the form. This data is forwarded by email and is not stored in a database on this site.

sections.heading: 4. Browsing data and cookies
sections.body: Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights collect aggregated usage metrics without cookies. Google Analytics and Google Ads only load after you accept the cookie banner, and can be turned off at any time from the link in the footer.

sections.heading: 5. Preferences saved in your browser
sections.body: Your browser stores theme and language preferences, your cookie choice, and caches of public GitHub information. After authorization, campaign parameters and advertising identifiers may be stored for the session. Revoking authorization from the footer removes this attribution and Google cookies accessible to the site.

sections.heading: 6. Sharing and international data transfer
sections.body: The site uses Vercel for hosting and operational metrics, Resend for sending emails, the contact inbox provider for receiving messages, Google for analytics and advertising when authorized, and Cloudflare Turnstile for spam protection when enabled. When shared rate limiting is configured, Upstash receives an HMAC-protected identifier derived from the IP, expiring within one hour. Providers may process data outside Brazil. Applicable contractual transfer mechanisms must be verified under LGPD art. 33 and ANPD regulations; details can be requested through the privacy contact.

sections.heading: 7. Your rights as a data subject
sections.body: Under LGPD art. 18, you can request confirmation that processing exists, access, correction of incomplete or outdated data, anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data, portability, information about sharing with third parties, and you can revoke consent at any time, via contato@pedrotx.com.br. If you're not satisfied with the response, you can also file a complaint with Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) at gov.br/anpd.

sections.heading: 8. Retention
sections.body: Messages remain in the email inbox until manually deleted. Deletion requests can be sent to contato@pedrotx.com.br and will be evaluated considering their purpose and any retention obligations. Form content is not saved in an application database. Abuse prevention counters expire within one hour; browser campaign data lasts for the session or until consent is revoked.

sections.heading: 9. Security
sections.body: The site uses HTTPS and security headers to protect data in transit. In the event of a security incident that could pose relevant risk to data subjects, notification will follow LGPD art. 48.

sections.heading: 10. Minors
sections.body: This site is not directed at anyone under 18 and does not knowingly collect data from children or teenagers without a legal guardian's specific consent.

sections.heading: 11. Changes
sections.body: This policy may be updated at any time. The date at the top of this page reflects the latest version.

sections.heading: 12. Contact
sections.body: To exercise your rights or ask about this policy, write to contato@pedrotx.com.br.
